summary:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator

Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive web application designed to help mission planners explore and compare potential landing locations near the Moon’s South Pole. The platform uses lunar terrain data and astronomical calculations to evaluate important mission conditions, including sunlight visibility, Earth visibility, and terrain obstruction over a selected time period.

Users can explore a 3D model of the Moon, locate candidate landing sites, and examine their surrounding terrain. The application also provides scientific visualizations and site comparisons to help identify locations that may offer more favorable conditions for future lunar missions.

By combining interactive 3D visualization, data analysis, and site recommendations, our project aims to make complex lunar environmental information easier to understand and support more informed landing-site selection.
details:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive web application developed to help users explore and compare potential landing sites near the Moon’s South Pole. Finding a suitable landing location is challenging because each site has different environmental conditions, and these conditions can change over time. Sunlight availability, Earth visibility, and the surrounding terrain are important factors that may affect future lunar missions.

Our platform brings these factors together in one place. It uses lunar terrain data and astronomical calculations to study how the Sun and Earth appear from different locations on the lunar surface. It also considers the effect of nearby mountains, craters, and other terrain features that may block the view of these objects. Users can select a landing site, choose a mission time period, and explore the results through interactive graphs and a 3D Moon model.

The platform also allows users to compare different candidate sites based on their sunlight and Earth visibility conditions. By turning complex scientific data into clear visual information, our project aims to make lunar site exploration easier and support better-informed decisions for future Moon missions.
